title: Texas's 31st Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for Texas's 31st Congressional District features 84-year-old Republican incumbent John Carter, who has held the seat since the district's creation in 2003, against Democratic nominee Justin Early, a cybersecurity architect and U.S. Army veteran. The district covers parts of Central Texas including Williamson County, Bell County (home to Fort Hood), and portions of six other counties. Cook Political Report rates this race as 'Solid Republican,' reflecting the district's Republican-leaning Partisan Voting Index of R+11. Carter defeated a crowded primary field with nearly 60% of the vote, while Early won the Democratic primary with 57.6%.
polling_note: No public general election polls were found for this race as of this search. Cook Political Report rates the race as Solid Republican.

candidates.name: John Carter
candidates.summary: John Carter is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 31st Congressional District, first elected in 2002. He previously served as a state district judge in Williamson County for 20 years. In Congress, he chairs the Military Construction and Veterans Affairs Subcommittee on Appropriations and has focused on military, veterans, homeland security, and fiscal issues.

candidates.name: Justin Early
candidates.summary: Justin Early is a cybersecurity architect at Dell Technologies and a U.S. Army veteran who served as a paratrooper at Fort Bragg and at the Defense Intelligence Agency at the Pentagon following the 9/11 attacks. He won the Democratic primary for Texas's 31st Congressional District with 57.6% of the vote, defeating Stuart Whitlow. His campaign focuses on supporting labor unions, veterans, career and technical education, and protecting Social Security and Medicare.
